seoTitle: Herschel Walker Trade Verdict | Cowboys vs Vikings
seoDescription: The Herschel Walker trade helped build a Dallas dynasty and remains one of the most consequential deals in NFL history. TradeVerdicts examines the long-term outcome.
headline: The Herschel Walker Trade: The Deal That Changed NFL History
dek: Dallas transformed one superstar running back into the foundation of a championship dynasty, while Minnesota paid one of the largest prices ever seen for a single player.

sections.heading: Why the Vikings Made the Trade
sections.body: Minnesota believed it was one player away from a Super Bowl. Herschel Walker was one of the biggest stars in football and one of the most physically gifted running backs of his era. The Vikings viewed him as the final piece capable of pushing an already talented roster over the top. At the time, the logic was understandable. Elite running backs were considered franchise-changing assets, and Walker's reputation made the aggressive price appear justified.

sections.heading: What Dallas Actually Received
sections.body: The trade is often remembered as a Herschel Walker deal, but the true story is the collection of assets Dallas acquired. The Cowboys gained players, draft choices, and conditional compensation that ultimately became far more valuable than Walker himself. While Minnesota focused on acquiring a star, Dallas focused on accumulating resources. That difference in philosophy would define the outcome.

sections.heading: How Jimmy Johnson Built a Dynasty
sections.body: The Cowboys did not simply collect draft picks. They converted those assets into cornerstone players who became the backbone of multiple Super Bowl teams. The flexibility created by the Walker trade allowed Dallas to accelerate its rebuild and construct one of the greatest rosters of the modern era. Few trades in professional sports history have had such a direct connection to future championships.

sections.heading: Why the Deal Failed for Minnesota
sections.body: Walker remained a productive player, but the Vikings never received the transformational impact they envisioned when making the trade. More importantly, Minnesota surrendered an enormous amount of long-term value in the process. The Vikings sacrificed future roster-building flexibility and ultimately failed to reach the Super Bowl during Walker's tenure. As Dallas improved, the opportunity cost of the deal became increasingly difficult to ignore.

sections.heading: The Long-Term Legacy
sections.body: More than three decades later, the Herschel Walker trade remains the benchmark for blockbuster NFL deals. Every major trade involving large draft compensation is inevitably compared to it. The transaction fundamentally altered the trajectory of both franchises and serves as a lasting lesson about the risks of concentrating enormous value into a single player acquisition.

sections.heading: Final Verdict
sections.body: This remains one of the clearest verdicts in NFL history. Dallas converted a star player into the foundation of a dynasty and multiple championships. Minnesota acquired a household name but never achieved the ultimate goal that justified the cost. The Cowboys' return reshaped the league and continues to stand as one of the greatest trade outcomes ever recorded.

seoTitle: A.J. Brown to the Patriots Trade Verdict
seoDescription: New England acquired A.J. Brown in one of the biggest receiver trades of the modern NFL era. TradeVerdicts examines the long-term implications for both franchises.
headline: A.J. Brown to the Patriots: A Franchise-Altering Trade Verdict
dek: New England acquired one of football's premier receivers, while Philadelphia chose future assets, roster flexibility, and a different competitive timeline.

sections.heading: One of the Biggest Receiver Trades in Years
sections.body: Elite wide receivers rarely become available while still performing at a high level. A.J. Brown had already established himself as one of the NFL's most productive offensive weapons, capable of changing defensive game plans every week. New England was not acquiring a developmental prospect or a speculative asset. The Patriots were acquiring a proven star who could instantly reshape the ceiling of an offense. Philadelphia, meanwhile, made the difficult decision to exchange established production for flexibility and future value.

sections.heading: Why New England Made the Move
sections.body: For the Patriots, the appeal was straightforward. Proven elite talent carries less uncertainty than future draft selections or developmental players. Brown offered immediate impact, proven production, and the ability to elevate the players around him. Organizations often spend years searching for a true No. 1 receiver. New England determined that Brown's proven value outweighed the assets required to acquire him.

sections.heading: Why Philadelphia Accepted the Deal
sections.body: Philadelphia's side of the trade reflects a different roster-building philosophy. Rather than concentrating resources in a single player, the Eagles chose flexibility and additional opportunities to build long-term value. The success of Philadelphia's approach will ultimately depend on what becomes of the acquired resources. Replacing a receiver of Brown's caliber is rarely simple, and that challenge will define the long-term evaluation of the Eagles' decision.

sections.heading: Final Verdict
sections.body: The Patriots receive the stronger long-term grade because they acquired the most difficult asset to obtain in professional football: a proven elite player performing at a high level. Philadelphia gained flexibility and future opportunities, but those assets must eventually develop into meaningful production before the trade can truly be judged as equal value. Unless the return dramatically exceeds expectations, New England's acquisition of A.J. Brown is likely to remain the defining outcome of this transaction.

seoTitle: Myles Garrett to the Rams Trade Verdict
seoDescription: The Rams acquired Myles Garrett in one of the biggest defensive trades in NFL history. TradeVerdicts breaks down the long-term winner.
headline: Myles Garrett to the Rams: One of the Biggest Defensive Trades Ever
dek: Los Angeles paid a massive price for a generational pass rusher, while Cleveland chose a package built around Jared Verse and future draft capital.

sections.heading: One of the Biggest Defensive Trades in NFL History
sections.body: Elite pass rushers almost never become available in their prime, and Myles Garrett was more than merely elite. The Rams did not acquire a rebuilding piece or a developmental prospect. They acquired a player capable of changing offensive game plans every week. That reality alone places this transaction among the most significant defensive trades of the modern era.

sections.heading: Why the Rams Went All In
sections.body: The Rams have spent the better part of a decade operating under a simple philosophy: when a championship window opens, attack it aggressively. Los Angeles viewed Garrett as the type of player who could transform an already strong roster into a Super Bowl favorite. For a franchise with championship aspirations, Garrett represented certainty in a league filled with uncertainty.

sections.heading: Why Cleveland Accepted the Deal
sections.body: From Cleveland's perspective, the decision centered on long-term value. Trading a franchise icon is never popular, but the Browns extracted one of the strongest defensive trade packages seen in years. Jared Verse arrived as a young cornerstone player rather than a speculative asset, and Cleveland also secured multiple premium draft selections.

sections.heading: Final Verdict
sections.body: This trade illustrates the tension between proven greatness and future flexibility. Cleveland received a substantial return, but history tends to favor teams that acquire truly elite players. Garrett was not merely a star; he was arguably the most impactful defensive player in football when the deal occurred. For now, the Rams earn the stronger grade because they acquired a proven generational talent.

seoTitle: Jonathan Greenard to the Eagles Trade Verdict
seoDescription: Philadelphia acquired Jonathan Greenard from Minnesota in a win-now move designed to strengthen an already dangerous defense.
headline: Jonathan Greenard to the Eagles: An Aggressive Championship Push
dek: Philadelphia added one of the NFL's most productive edge rushers, while Minnesota chose future assets and roster flexibility.

sections.heading: Why This Trade Matters
sections.body: Pass rush remains one of the most valuable commodities in football, and Jonathan Greenard entered this trade as one of the league's most productive edge defenders. After helping anchor Minnesota's defense, Greenard became the centerpiece of a deal that signaled Philadelphia's intention to maximize its championship window.

sections.heading: Why Philadelphia Made the Move
sections.body: The Eagles approached this trade from a position of contention. Teams with legitimate championship aspirations often place greater value on proven production than future possibilities. Greenard offered immediate pass-rush help, defensive versatility, and a track record of disruptive play.

sections.heading: Why Minnesota Accepted the Deal
sections.body: From Minnesota's perspective, the trade represented a long-term roster decision rather than a simple talent evaluation. The Vikings understood Greenard's value, but they also recognized the opportunity to convert a veteran asset into future flexibility.

sections.heading: Final Verdict
sections.body: Philadelphia receives the stronger immediate grade because it acquired the most proven asset in the transaction. Minnesota's side cannot be dismissed because future assets can create significant long-term value, but that value remains uncertain until it develops into production.

seoTitle: D.J. Moore to the Bills Trade Verdict
seoDescription: Buffalo acquired D.J. Moore in a major receiver trade designed to strengthen its offense. TradeVerdicts breaks down the deal.
headline: D.J. Moore to the Bills: Buffalo Adds a Proven Offensive Weapon
dek: Buffalo added a veteran receiver with proven production, while the other side chose flexibility, draft value, and a reset at the position.

sections.heading: Why This Trade Matters
sections.body: Receiver trades can reshape an offense quickly, and D.J. Moore brought Buffalo a proven playmaker rather than a projection. Moore had already shown he could produce through changing quarterback situations and shifting offensive structures. That kind of reliability matters for a team trying to maximize a competitive window.

sections.heading: Why Buffalo Made the Move
sections.body: Buffalo's logic was straightforward: add a proven target who could help immediately. Rather than waiting for a draft pick or younger player to develop, the Bills acquired a receiver with established NFL production. Moore gave Buffalo another way to stress defenses and another dependable option in high-leverage situations.

sections.heading: What the Other Side Was Betting On
sections.body: The selling side chose flexibility over certainty. Moving a veteran receiver can create cap room, draft value, and a cleaner long-term roster structure. That approach can work, but only if the return becomes meaningful production. The value of moving Moore depends entirely on what the acquired assets become.

sections.heading: Final Verdict
sections.body: Buffalo earns the stronger immediate verdict because it acquired the proven player. Moore's production was already established, while the value going the other direction required projection. Unless the return develops into clear long-term contributors, the Bills' decision to secure a reliable offensive weapon will remain the defining outcome.

seoTitle: Jaylen Waddle to the Broncos Trade Verdict
seoDescription: Denver acquired Jaylen Waddle in a speed-driven offensive trade with Miami. TradeVerdicts examines the long-term winner.
headline: Jaylen Waddle to the Broncos: Denver Pays for Explosive Speed
dek: Denver acquired one of the league's most dangerous speed receivers, while Miami converted a major offensive piece into future roster flexibility.

sections.heading: Why This Trade Matters
sections.body: Few traits change defensive spacing like elite speed. Jaylen Waddle brought Denver a player who could alter coverage rules, stretch the field, and create explosive plays without needing a perfect offensive environment. That made this trade more than a simple receiver swap. It was a bet on offensive ceiling.

sections.heading: Why Denver Made the Move
sections.body: Denver was buying explosiveness. Waddle's value comes from the pressure he puts on a defense before the ball is even snapped. Players with that kind of speed can create opportunities for teammates, open underneath windows, and punish defenses that make mistakes.

sections.heading: Why Miami Accepted the Deal
sections.body: Miami's side reflects the difficult math of roster construction. Moving a dynamic receiver is painful, but it can create flexibility and return value that helps the broader roster. The decision only works if the Dolphins convert the acquired assets into real production.

sections.heading: Final Verdict
sections.body: Denver receives the stronger immediate grade because Waddle was the rarest asset in the trade: a proven explosive playmaker. Miami gained future value and flexibility, but those benefits remain theoretical until they become production. For now, the Broncos' acquisition of Waddle carries the clearer upside.

seoDescription: Trent McDuffie became the centerpiece of a major defensive back trade. TradeVerdicts breaks down the long-term value.
headline: Trent McDuffie Trade Verdict: The Value of an Elite Cornerback
dek: This deal centered on one of football's most valuable defensive assets: a proven cover corner capable of changing how opponents attack.

sections.heading: Why This Trade Matters
sections.body: Cornerback is one of the hardest positions to solve in the NFL, and Trent McDuffie represented a premium answer. Reliable coverage defenders are difficult to find, expensive to replace, and essential against modern passing offenses. Any trade involving a player of McDuffie's caliber deserves elevated attention.

sections.heading: The Case for Acquiring McDuffie
sections.body: The team acquiring McDuffie was buying proven defensive stability. Rather than projecting a draft pick into a future role, the acquiring side added a player who had already demonstrated high-level coverage ability. In the modern NFL, that kind of certainty carries major value.

sections.heading: The Case for Moving McDuffie
sections.body: The team moving McDuffie chose asset flexibility over retaining a premium defender. That can be logical if the return helps address multiple roster needs or creates long-term cap and draft flexibility. Still, moving an elite cornerback creates immediate defensive risk.

sections.heading: Final Verdict
sections.body: The side acquiring McDuffie holds the clearer immediate advantage because elite cornerbacks are scarce. The trade can become more balanced if the return develops into multiple valuable contributors, but the proven player carries the stronger verdict until that future value materializes.

seoTitle: Dexter Lawrence to the Bengals Trade Verdict
seoDescription: Cincinnati acquired Dexter Lawrence for the No. 10 pick used on Francis Mauigoa. TradeVerdicts reevaluates the blockbuster for both teams.
headline: Dexter Lawrence to the Bengals: Cincinnati Lands a Defensive Centerpiece
dek: Cincinnati acquired a proven elite interior defender, while New York converted Lawrence into the No. 10 pick and a cost-controlled offensive tackle in Francis Mauigoa.

sections.heading: A Rare Interior Difference-Maker
sections.body: Interior defenders who can defeat double teams, disrupt the run, and collapse a passing pocket are among the hardest players to acquire. Dexter Lawrence gave Cincinnati something a draft pick could not guarantee: established NFL dominance at the center of the defense. His presence could improve the players around him by creating cleaner opportunities and forcing offenses to change protection plans.

sections.heading: Why Cincinnati Paid the Price
sections.body: The Bengals surrendered the No. 10 pick, but they did not surrender a package of multiple first-round selections. Cincinnati chose certainty over projection and acquired a player already capable of performing at an elite level. For a team seeking immediate defensive improvement, the opportunity to add Lawrence justified an aggressive move.

sections.heading: Why New York Chose Mauigoa
sections.body: The Giants converted Lawrence into Francis Mauigoa, a premium tackle prospect with the potential to anchor the offensive line for years. Offensive tackle is an expensive and difficult position to solve. A successful top-10 selection can provide high-level play and major contractual value throughout a rookie deal.

sections.heading: The Value of a Top-10 Tackle
sections.body: New York's return should not be dismissed as merely one draft pick. The No. 10 selection gave the Giants access to a prospect at a cornerstone position and five years of cost control. That is meaningful roster-building value. It also explains why the Giants deserve a B- rather than the previous D+, even though the return remains unproven.

sections.heading: The Risk on Both Sides
sections.body: Cincinnati assumed the financial and age-related risk attached to an established veteran, while New York assumed developmental risk. The Bengals need Lawrence to remain a dominant force. The Giants need Mauigoa to become a long-term starter. Cincinnati's outcome is easier to project, which is why the Bengals receive the stronger grade today.

sections.heading: Final Verdict
sections.body: The Bengals win the current evaluation because they acquired the best player and the most certain football value for one premium pick. Cincinnati earns an A-. New York earns a B- because a top-10 tackle prospect on a rookie contract is a legitimate return, not a giveaway. The Giants can improve their side of the verdict if Mauigoa develops into a foundational offensive lineman.

headline: The 2007 Marcus Thomas Trade: Broncos Move Up, Vikings Bank Future Value
dek: Denver moved up for defensive tackle Marcus Thomas, while Minnesota turned the move down into two late picks and a future third-rounder that later became part of a much bigger roster-building chain.

headline: The 1985 Issiac Holt Deal: A Strange Draft-Day Side Agreement With Houston
dek: Minnesota recovered the No. 30 pick and selected Issiac Holt after agreeing not to block Houston's path to Ray Childress, making this one of the NFL draft's more unusual conditional transactions.

headline: The 2001 Broncos-Falcons Pick Swap: Three Sevenths for a Future Fourth
dek: Denver traded three seventh-round picks to Atlanta for a 2002 fourth-rounder. Atlanta's best result was guard Kynan Forney, a rare late-round starter who gave the Falcons years of value.

headline: The 2003 Ricky Manning Jr. Trade: Carolina's Move Up Paid Off in January
dek: Carolina moved up to No. 82 for Ricky Manning Jr., and the rookie cornerback became a postseason difference-maker during the Panthers' run to Super Bowl XXXVIII.

headline: The 2010 Brandon Graham Trade: Philadelphia Paid Up and Found a Franchise Eagle
dek: Philadelphia jumped from No. 24 to No. 13 for Brandon Graham. The price was substantial, but Graham's 15-year Eagles career and championship impact made the move age exceptionally well.

headline: The 2015 Shane Ray Trade: Denver Bought a Pass Rusher, Detroit Bought Volume
dek: Denver moved up five spots for Shane Ray, sending Detroit a first-rounder, two fifth-rounders and Manny Ramirez. Ray contributed to a title team, but the premium price limited Denver's long-term return.

headline: The 2011 Colin Kaepernick Trade: San Francisco Turned Three Picks Into a Super Bowl QB
dek: San Francisco sent picks 45, 108 and 141 to Denver to move up for Colin Kaepernick, a gamble that soon produced a Super Bowl appearance and another NFC title-game run.

headline: The 2009 Jay Cutler Trade: Chicago Got Its Quarterback, Denver Got the Asset Haul
dek: Chicago paid Kyle Orton, two first-round picks and a third-rounder for Jay Cutler and a fifth. The Bears gained years of quarterback production; Denver gained far more draft capital.

headline: The 2022 Andrew Booth Trade: Indianapolis Turned One Pick Into Three Contributors
dek: Minnesota moved up to No. 42 for Andrew Booth Jr.; Indianapolis moved down and came away with Alec Pierce, Bernhard Raimann and Andrew Ogletree.

headline: The 2000 Bears-Browns Seventh-Round Swap: A Low-Stakes Draft Shuffle
dek: Chicago and Cleveland reshuffled five late seventh-round selections. The transaction produced little lasting NFL value on either side, making the margin between winner and loser extremely small.

headline: The 2025 Broncos-Eagles Trade: Denver Moved Back Into Day 2 for Sai'vion Jones
dek: Denver sent three later picks to Philadelphia for Nos. 101 and 134, using them on Sai'vion Jones and Que Robinson. The long-term winner is still too early to call with confidence.

headline: The 2017 Jay Ajayi Trade: A Fourth-Round Pick Helped Philadelphia Win a Super Bowl
dek: Philadelphia paid a fourth-round pick for Jay Ajayi at the 2017 deadline, and the running back immediately became part of the rotation that carried the Eagles through their first Super Bowl title run.

headline: The 2020 Darius Slay Trade: Philadelphia Bought a No. 1 Corner for Mid-Round Picks
dek: Philadelphia paid third- and fifth-round picks for Darius Slay and immediately gave him a major extension. The veteran corner delivered Pro Bowl-level play and became a centerpiece of the Eagles secondary.

headline: The 2014 Kyle Van Noy Trade: Detroit Moved Up, Seattle Spread the Value Around
dek: Detroit climbed five spots for Kyle Van Noy and also received a fifth-rounder. Seattle took Paul Richardson, Kiero Small and additional draft value, creating a deal whose winner was narrower than the headline suggests.

headline: The 1984 Browns-Bears USFL Rights Trade: Kevin Mack Became the Difference
dek: Cleveland acquired the USFL rights that became Kevin Mack, Gerald McNeil and Doug West. Chicago received four late-round NFL picks and found a real keeper of its own in Shaun Gayle.

headline: The 1994 Warren Moon Trade: Minnesota Bought Two Pro Bowl Seasons for Mid-Round Picks
dek: Minnesota sent a 1994 fourth-rounder and a 1995 third-rounder to Houston for Warren Moon. The Hall of Fame quarterback immediately delivered record-setting passing production and two Pro Bowl seasons.

headline: The 2022 Amari Cooper Trade: Cleveland Bought a No. 1 Receiver for a Fifth-Round Pick
dek: Cleveland sent Dallas a fifth-round pick and swapped sixth-rounders for Amari Cooper. Cooper answered with back-to-back 1,000-yard seasons and one of the best receiving games in Browns history.

headline: The 1999 Champ Bailey Trade: Washington Gave Up Volume and Drafted a Hall of Famer
dek: Chicago moved from No. 7 to No. 12 and collected four additional picks. Washington moved back up for Champ Bailey, whose Hall of Fame career overwhelmed the Bears' larger package.

headline: The 2014 DeMarcus Lawrence Trade: Dallas Paid Two Picks for a Decade-Long Defensive Anchor
dek: Dallas sent picks 47 and 78 to Washington for No. 34 and selected DeMarcus Lawrence. Washington landed Trent Murphy and Spencer Long, but Lawrence became the defining player in the deal.

headline: The 1990 Steve Walsh Trade: Dallas Turned a Backup Quarterback Into Dynasty Capital
dek: New Orleans sent Dallas first-, third- and second-round picks for Steve Walsh. The third-rounder became Erik Williams, and the larger package gave the Cowboys more ammunition during their dynasty build.

headline: The 1990 Emmitt Smith Trade: Dallas Moved Four Spots and Found a Dynasty Centerpiece
dek: Dallas moved from No. 21 to No. 17 for Emmitt Smith, sending Pittsburgh an extra third-round pick. The Steelers found a Pro Bowl tight end in Eric Green, but Smith became an all-time great.

headline: The 2016 Sam Bradford Trade: Minnesota Bought Emergency Stability, Philadelphia Bought the Future
dek: Minnesota sent a 2017 first-rounder and a 2018 fourth-rounder to Philadelphia after Teddy Bridgewater's knee injury. Bradford played well immediately, but the Eagles ultimately held the stronger asset return.

headline: The 2010 Bryant McFadden Trade: Pittsburgh Got a Starter Back and the Pick That Became Antonio Brown
dek: Pittsburgh sent a fifth-round pick to Arizona for Bryant McFadden and a sixth-rounder. The corner returned to the starting lineup, and pick No. 195 became Antonio Brown.

headline: The 2000 Joey Galloway Trade: Seattle Turned One Receiver Into Two First-Round Picks
dek: Dallas paid first-round picks in 2000 and 2001 for Joey Galloway. Seattle used the first on Shaun Alexander, the future league MVP, and retained another premium first-round asset.

headline: The 2001 Trent Green Trade: Kansas City Bought Its Quarterback With the No. 12 Pick
dek: Kansas City sent the 12th overall pick to St. Louis for Trent Green and a fifth-rounder. Green became the engine of Dick Vermeil's offense and gave the Chiefs years of high-level quarterback stability.

headline: The 2019 Robert Quinn Trade: Dallas Bought 11.5 Sacks for a Sixth-Round Pick
dek: Dallas sent Miami a future sixth-rounder for Robert Quinn and received a one-year pass-rush surge. Quinn led the Cowboys with 11.5 sacks before leaving in free agency.

headline: The 2022 A.J. Brown Trade: Philadelphia Turned Two Draft Picks Into a Franchise Receiver
dek: Philadelphia sent Tennessee picks 18 and 101 for A.J. Brown, then signed him long term. Brown immediately transformed the Eagles passing game and became a centerpiece of a championship era.

headline: The 2013 Alex Smith Trade: Kansas City Bought Stability and Built the Bridge to Mahomes
dek: Kansas City sent San Francisco two second-round picks for Alex Smith. He helped reverse a 2-14 team immediately, made three Pro Bowls as a Chief and stabilized the franchise before Patrick Mahomes took over.

headline: The 2022 C.J. Gardner-Johnson Trade: Philadelphia Found a League-Leading Ballhawk for Late Picks
dek: Philadelphia acquired C.J. Gardner-Johnson and a seventh-rounder from New Orleans for fifth- and sixth-round selections. He tied for the NFL lead with six interceptions during a Super Bowl run.

headline: The 1992 Charles Haley Trade: Dallas Acquired the Final Piece of a Dynasty
dek: Dallas sent San Francisco second- and third-round picks for Charles Haley. The pass rusher immediately transformed the Cowboys defense and helped deliver three Super Bowl titles in four seasons.

headline: The 1988 Neil Smith Trade: Kansas City Landed a Star, but Detroit Landed Two Cornerstones
dek: Kansas City paid the third and 29th picks to move to No. 2 for Neil Smith. Smith became a Chiefs legend, but Detroit answered with Bennie Blades and Chris Spielman.

headline: The 2005 Randy Moss Trade: Oakland Got the Superstar, but Neither Side Maximized the Deal
dek: Minnesota sent Randy Moss to Oakland for Napoleon Harris, the No. 7 pick and a seventh-rounder. The Vikings botched the draft return, while Moss's Raiders stint lasted only two uneven seasons.

headline: The 2007 Brian Robison Trade: Minnesota Moved Four Spots and Found an 11-Year Viking
dek: Minnesota sent picks 106 and 182 to Tampa Bay for No. 102 and selected Brian Robison. The fourth-round move produced 173 games, 60 sacks and more than a decade of defensive-line stability.

headline: The 2012 Harrison Smith Trade: Minnesota Moved Back Into Round 1 and Found a Franchise Safety
dek: Minnesota sent picks 35 and 98 to Baltimore for No. 29 and selected Harrison Smith. The move produced a six-time Pro Bowler and one of the most accomplished defenders in Vikings history.

headline: The 2023 Brandin Cooks Trade: Dallas Added a Proven Receiver for Two Late Picks
dek: Dallas acquired Brandin Cooks from Houston for a fifth-rounder and a future sixth. Cooks gave the Cowboys eight touchdowns in his first season and veteran speed opposite CeeDee Lamb.

headline: The 2001 Casey Hampton Trade: Pittsburgh Moved Down, Added Picks and Found Its Nose Tackle
dek: Pittsburgh dropped from No. 16 to No. 19, added fourth- and sixth-round picks and still drafted Casey Hampton. Hampton became a five-time Pro Bowler and a cornerstone of two Super Bowl winners.

headline: The 1974 John Matuszak Trade: Houston Turned One Deal Into Two Hall of Famers
dek: Houston sent John Matuszak and a future third-round pick to Kansas City for Curley Culp and the first-round pick that became Robert Brazile. The Oilers built the spine of a great defense in one transaction.

headline: The 2016 Maxwell-Alonso Trade: Miami Found Tunsil, Philadelphia Found Its Route to Wentz
dek: Miami moved from No. 8 to No. 13 and added Byron Maxwell and Kiko Alonso. Philadelphia escaped two contracts and used the No. 8 pick as the launching point for its move to Carson Wentz.

headline: The 2010 Jahvid Best Trade: Detroit Chased Explosiveness, Minnesota Found Everson Griffen
dek: Detroit moved back into the first round for Jahvid Best. Minnesota moved down and came away with Chris Cook, Everson Griffen and another late pick, giving the Vikings the stronger long-term return.

headline: The 1996 Jerome Bettis Trade: Pittsburgh Bought a Hall of Fame Identity for Two Picks
dek: Pittsburgh acquired Jerome Bettis and a third-rounder from the Rams for a second-round pick and a future fourth. Bettis spent 10 seasons as a Steeler and retired after a Super Bowl championship.

headline: The 2010 Dez Bryant-Devin McCourty Trade: Both Teams Found Franchise Players
dek: Dallas moved from No. 27 to No. 24 for Dez Bryant, while New England dropped three spots for Devin McCourty and added a third-round pick. Both clubs landed players who defined the next decade.

headline: The 1967 Fran Tarkenton Trade: The Giants Got a Star, Minnesota Built a Contender
dek: New York acquired Fran Tarkenton for four premium draft picks. Minnesota used the return on Clint Jones, Bob Grim, Ron Yary and Ed White, helping build the roster that dominated the NFC in the 1970s.

headline: The 2021 DeVonta Smith-Micah Parsons Trade: Philadelphia Got Its Receiver, Dallas Got a Superstar
dek: Philadelphia moved from No. 12 to No. 10 for DeVonta Smith. Dallas moved back, selected Micah Parsons and added Chauncey Golston, creating one of the rare draft trades where both sides landed stars.

headline: The 2000 Joey Galloway Trade: Seattle Turned One Receiver Into Shaun Alexander and Another First
dek: Dallas sent consecutive first-round picks to Seattle for Joey Galloway. The Seahawks used those selections on Shaun Alexander and Koren Robinson, while Galloway lost his first Cowboys season to a torn ACL.

headline: The 2008 Roy Williams Trade: Detroit Sold at Peak Value and Dallas Paid a First-Round Price
dek: Dallas sent first-, third- and sixth-round picks to Detroit for Roy Williams and a seventh. The Lions turned the first into Brandon Pettigrew, while Williams never became the Cowboys' expected No. 1 target.

headline: The 2008 Jared Allen Trade: Minnesota Bought an Elite Pass Rusher, Kansas City Drafted Jamaal Charles
dek: Minnesota paid a first-rounder, two thirds and a sixth-round swap for Jared Allen. Allen delivered 85.5 sacks in six Vikings seasons, while Kansas City used one of the picks on Jamaal Charles.

headline: The 2013 Percy Harvin Trade: Minnesota Built a Draft Haul, Seattle Bought a Super Bowl Moment
dek: Seattle sent Minnesota first-, seventh- and future third-round picks for Percy Harvin. The Vikings landed Xavier Rhodes and Jerick McKinnon; Harvin's Seattle tenure was brief but included an iconic Super Bowl touchdown.

headline: The 2021 Dolphins-Eagles Trade: Miami Got Jaylen Waddle, Philadelphia Built a First-Round Asset Chain
dek: Miami moved from No. 12 to No. 6 for Jaylen Waddle. Philadelphia moved down, added a future first and still maneuvered back up for DeVonta Smith, giving both teams cornerstone value.

headline: The 2019 Frank Clark Trade: Kansas City Paid a Premium for a Championship Pass Rusher
dek: Kansas City sent Seattle a first-round pick and more draft value for Frank Clark, then made him a centerpiece of a defense that helped the Chiefs win championships.

headline: The 1992 Cowboys-Patriots Draft Trade: Dallas Moved Down and Found Darren Woodson
dek: New England climbed from No. 19 to No. 13, while Dallas added the second-round pick that became Darren Woodson and built the stronger long-term return.

headline: The 2020 Stefon Diggs Trade: Buffalo Got Its No. 1 Receiver, Minnesota Drafted Justin Jefferson
dek: Buffalo paid a first-round-centered package for Stefon Diggs, while Minnesota used the No. 22 pick on Justin Jefferson. Both teams immediately got the star they needed.

headline: The 1997 Tony Gonzalez Trade-Up: Kansas City Moved Five Spots for a Hall of Fame Tight End
dek: Kansas City climbed from No. 18 to No. 13 to draft Tony Gonzalez. The Oilers collected extra picks, but the Chiefs secured one of the greatest tight ends in NFL history.

headline: The 2016 Carson Wentz Trade: Philadelphia Paid a Huge Draft Price and Opened a Super Bowl Window
dek: Philadelphia sent Cleveland a five-pick package to reach No. 2 for Carson Wentz. The price was enormous, but Wentz's 2017 season helped put the Eagles in championship position.

headline: The 2023 Jalen Carter Trade-Up: Philadelphia Got an Elite Defender, Chicago Got Darnell Wright
dek: Philadelphia moved from No. 10 to No. 9 for Jalen Carter and sent Chicago a future fourth. The Bears used No. 10 on Darnell Wright, giving both teams a core building block.

headline: The 2022 Saints-Eagles Draft Trade: Philadelphia Turned Patience Into a Future Top-10 Pick
dek: New Orleans acquired two 2022 first-rounders, while Philadelphia pushed major value into 2023 and 2024. The future first became the key asset in the Eagles' move for Jalen Carter.

headline: The 2010 Demaryius Thomas Trade-Up: Denver Found a Star While New England Kept Dealing
dek: Denver sent New England picks No. 24 and No. 113 to reach No. 22 for Demaryius Thomas. The Patriots moved the first-rounder again, making this a rare value-rich deal on both sides.

headline: The 1984 Earl Campbell Trade: New Orleans Paid a First-Round Pick for the End of a Great Career
dek: The Saints reunited Earl Campbell with Bum Phillips, but Houston received a 1985 first-round pick for a running back whose dominant seasons were already behind him.

headline: The 2013 Trent Richardson Trade: Cleveland Recovered a First-Round Pick Before the Value Collapsed
dek: Indianapolis sent Cleveland a 2014 first-round pick for Trent Richardson only 17 games into his career. The Browns sold early, and Richardson never regained first-round value.

headline: The 2016 Jamie Collins Trade: New England Chose Draft Value Over an Expiring Star Linebacker
dek: New England sent Jamie Collins to Cleveland at the trade deadline for a conditional draft pick. The Browns got immediate production, but a costly extension shortened the payoff.

headline: The 2007 Randy Moss Trade: New England Bought a Record-Breaking Season for a Fourth-Round Pick
dek: Oakland sent Randy Moss to New England for the 110th pick in the 2007 draft. Moss responded with 23 receiving touchdowns as the Patriots went 16-0 in the regular season.

headline: The 1996 Sean Gilbert Trade: Washington Turned the No. 6 Pick Into an Established Defensive Lineman
dek: Washington sent the sixth overall pick to St. Louis for Sean Gilbert. The Rams used it on Lawrence Phillips, while Washington later extracted even more value from Gilbert.

headline: The 1978 Earl Campbell Trade: Houston Moved to No. 1 and Landed a Hall of Fame Centerpiece
dek: Houston traded with Tampa Bay for the first overall pick and selected Earl Campbell. The Buccaneers received real value, but the Oilers landed the defining player.

headline: The 2018 Amari Cooper Trade: Dallas Paid a First-Round Pick and Rescued Its Passing Game
dek: Dallas sent its 2019 first-round pick to Oakland for Amari Cooper. Cooper sparked the Cowboys immediately, while the Raiders used No. 27 on Johnathan Abram.

headline: The 1985 George Rogers Trade: Washington Bought a Proven Runner and Got a Super Bowl Contributor
dek: Washington sent New Orleans the 24th pick for George Rogers plus three later selections. Rogers delivered two 1,000-yard seasons and finished his career as a champion.

headline: The 2019 Antonio Brown Trade: Pittsburgh Got Two Picks for a Raider Who Never Played a Game
dek: Oakland sent Pittsburgh third- and fifth-round picks for Antonio Brown. The Steelers drafted Diontae Johnson and Zach Gentry; Brown was released before Week 1.

headline: The 1972 Fran Tarkenton Trade: Minnesota Paid a Huge Package to Bring Its Franchise Quarterback Home
dek: The Vikings reacquired Fran Tarkenton from the Giants for players and premium picks. Tarkenton later won league MVP and quarterbacked three Minnesota Super Bowl teams.

headline: The 2017 Kelvin Benjamin Trade: Carolina Sold at the Right Time and Collected Two Draft Picks
dek: Carolina moved Kelvin Benjamin to Buffalo at the deadline for third- and seventh-round picks. Benjamin never became the difference-maker the Bills expected.

headline: The 1995 Ki-Jana Carter Trade: Carolina Moved Off No. 1 and Cincinnati's Gamble Collapsed
dek: Cincinnati sent the fifth and 36th picks to expansion Carolina for No. 1 overall, then selected Ki-Jana Carter. Injuries turned the aggressive move into a costly miss.

headline: The 1993 Joe Montana Trade: Kansas City Spent a First-Round Pick to Become an Immediate AFC Contender
dek: Kansas City sent San Francisco the 18th pick for Joe Montana, David Whitmore and a future third. Montana immediately led the Chiefs to the AFC title game.

headline: The 1958 Bobby Layne Trade: Pittsburgh Acquired a Hall of Fame Quarterback and Changed Its Trajectory
dek: Detroit sent Bobby Layne to Pittsburgh for Earl Morrall and two draft choices. Layne immediately stabilized the Steelers and remained their starter through 1962.

headline: The 1983 Mike Haynes Deal: The Raiders Paid Premium Picks and Added a Hall of Fame Corner for a Title Run
dek: The Raiders acquired Mike Haynes during the 1983 season, while New England received first- and second-round compensation. Haynes helped win Super Bowl XVIII immediately.

headline: The 2007 Wes Welker Trade: New England Turned a Second and Seventh Into an Elite Volume Receiver
dek: Miami sent Wes Welker to New England for second- and seventh-round picks. Welker became one of Tom Brady's most productive targets and transformed the slot role.

headline: The 2011 Carson Palmer Trade: Cincinnati Turned a Holdout Into Two Premium Draft Picks
dek: Oakland paid a 2012 first-rounder and a conditional 2013 selection for Carson Palmer. Cincinnati converted a broken relationship into years of usable roster value.

headline: The 2020 DeAndre Hopkins Trade: Arizona Acquired an All-Pro Receiver at a Discount
dek: Arizona landed DeAndre Hopkins and a fourth-round pick for David Johnson plus second- and fourth-round selections, then received an immediate All-Pro season.

headline: The 1999 Marshall Faulk Trade: St. Louis Bought the Engine of the Greatest Show on Turf
dek: The Rams sent Indianapolis second- and fifth-round picks for Marshall Faulk. One season later, Faulk was a record-setting centerpiece of a Super Bowl champion.

headline: The 2017 Patrick Mahomes Trade-Up: Kansas City Paid Three Premium Picks and Changed NFL History
dek: Kansas City moved from No. 27 to No. 10 for Patrick Mahomes. Buffalo received Tre'Davious White and major draft value, but the Chiefs secured a dynasty quarterback.

headline: The 2004 Eli Manning-Philip Rivers Trade: San Diego Won the Package, New York Won the Championships
dek: The Chargers received Philip Rivers plus three draft picks, but the Giants acquired Eli Manning and ultimately won two Super Bowls with him at quarterback.

headline: The 1997 Rick Mirer Trade: Seattle Turned a Fading Quarterback Into First-Round Draft Capital
dek: Chicago sent the No. 11 pick to Seattle for Rick Mirer and a fourth-rounder. Seattle then used that first-round asset to help move up for Shawn Springs.

headline: The 2013 Darrelle Revis Trade: The Jets Sold an Injured Star for the Pick That Became Sheldon Richardson
dek: Tampa Bay acquired Darrelle Revis for the No. 13 pick and conditional 2014 compensation. Revis made one Pro Bowl there, but the Buccaneers released him after one season.

headline: The 2021 Carson Wentz Trade: Philadelphia Escaped the Contract and Turned the Return Into a First-Round Pick
dek: Indianapolis sent Philadelphia a 2021 third-rounder and a conditional 2022 pick for Carson Wentz. The condition became a first, and Wentz lasted one Colts season.

headline: The 2019 Minkah Fitzpatrick Trade: Pittsburgh Spent a First-Round Pick and Got Years of All-Pro Play
dek: Pittsburgh acquired 22-year-old Minkah Fitzpatrick from Miami for a package led by a 2020 first-rounder. He became an immediate All-Pro and long-term defensive centerpiece.

headline: The 2018 Josh Allen Trade-Up: Buffalo Paid Two Second-Rounders to End Its Quarterback Search
dek: Buffalo moved from No. 12 to No. 7 for Josh Allen, sending Tampa Bay two second-round picks. The Buccaneers built useful depth; the Bills found an MVP quarterback.

headline: The 1992 Brett Favre Trade: Green Bay Spent the No. 17 Pick on an Unknown Backup and Changed the Franchise
dek: Ron Wolf sent Atlanta the 17th overall pick for Brett Favre after Favre had thrown only five NFL passes. The gamble produced three MVPs and a championship era.

headline: The 2021 Stafford-Goff Trade: The Rams Bought a Super Bowl, Detroit Bought Its Rebuild
dek: Los Angeles sent Jared Goff, a third-rounder and two first-round picks for Matthew Stafford. The Rams won immediately; Detroit turned the return into a new core.

headline: The 1998 Ryan Leaf Trade-Up: San Diego Paid a Massive Premium to Move One Spot
dek: The Chargers moved from No. 3 to No. 2 for Ryan Leaf, giving Arizona two premium picks and two veterans. Leaf's collapse made the one-slot move historically costly.

headline: The 2018 Lamar Jackson Trade: Baltimore Moved Back Into Round 1 and Found Its Franchise Quarterback
dek: Baltimore sent Philadelphia second- and fourth-round value to reach No. 32 for Lamar Jackson. The Eagles got useful assets, but the Ravens landed an MVP quarterback.

headline: The 2003 Troy Polamalu Trade-Up: Pittsburgh Broke Tradition for a Hall of Fame Safety
dek: Pittsburgh moved from No. 27 to No. 16 for Troy Polamalu, sending Kansas City third- and sixth-round picks. The rare Steelers trade-up produced an all-time defender.

headline: The 1987 Steve Young Trade: San Francisco Bought a Hall of Fame Succession Plan for Two Picks
dek: The 49ers sent Tampa Bay second- and fourth-round picks plus cash for Steve Young. He first backed up Joe Montana, then became an MVP and Super Bowl champion.

headline: The 2019 Laremy Tunsil Trade: Miami Turned One Elite Tackle Into a Rebuilding War Chest
dek: Houston acquired Laremy Tunsil and Kenny Stills, while Miami received two first-round picks, a second-rounder and two players. The Dolphins gained enormous flexibility.

headline: The 1990 Jeff George Trade: Atlanta Sold the No. 1 Pick for Two Proven Stars and Another First
dek: Indianapolis moved to No. 1 for Jeff George by sending Atlanta Andre Rison, Chris Hinton, a fifth-rounder and a 1991 first. The Falcons received immediate proven talent.

headline: The 2017 Mitchell Trubisky Trade-Up: Chicago Paid San Francisco Three Picks to Move One Spot
dek: The Bears jumped from No. 3 to No. 2 for Mitchell Trubisky. San Francisco still drafted Solomon Thomas and added picks, including the asset that became Fred Warner.

headline: The 2022 Christian McCaffrey Trade: San Francisco Paid Four Picks for an Offensive Centerpiece
dek: The 49ers sent Carolina second-, third-, fourth- and fifth-round picks for Christian McCaffrey. He immediately became a centerpiece of a Super Bowl-caliber offense.

headline: The 2018 Khalil Mack Trade: Chicago Paid Two First-Rounders and Got an Immediate All-Pro
dek: Chicago acquired Khalil Mack plus later picks for a package led by two first-round selections. Mack transformed the defense immediately and powered a 12-win season.

headline: The 1981 Fred Dean Trade: San Francisco Added the Pass Rusher Who Helped Launch a Dynasty
dek: The 49ers acquired Fred Dean from San Diego during the 1981 season for draft compensation. He became an immediate impact pass rusher and a Super Bowl champion.

headline: The 2021 Orlando Brown Jr. Trade: Kansas City Rebuilt Left Tackle Without Sacrificing the Entire Draft
dek: Kansas City sent Baltimore a first-round-centered package for Orlando Brown Jr. but received Brown and the second-round pick that became Nick Bolton.

headline: The 2022 Deshaun Watson Trade: Houston Collected Three First-Round Picks and Reset the Franchise
dek: Cleveland sent Houston three first-round picks plus additional selections for Deshaun Watson. The Texans converted the package into years of rebuilding flexibility.

headline: The 2012 RGIII Trade: Washington Paid Three First-Round Picks for One Electric Season
dek: Washington moved from No. 6 to No. 2 for Robert Griffin III. The Rams received three first-round picks and a second, giving them the stronger long-term asset return.

headline: The 2020 Jamal Adams Trade: Seattle Paid Two First-Round Picks for a Short Peak
dek: Seattle sent the Jets two first-round picks, a third and Bradley McDougald for Jamal Adams and a fourth. New York ultimately received the stronger long-term value.

headline: The 2022 Russell Wilson Trade: Seattle Sold at the Right Time and Reset Its Roster
dek: Denver sent Seattle two firsts, two seconds, a fifth and three players for Russell Wilson and a fourth. The Seahawks turned the haul into multiple core starters.

headline: The 1999 Ricky Williams Trade: New Orleans Sent an Entire Draft for One Running Back
dek: Mike Ditka's Saints sent eight selections to Washington to move from No. 12 to No. 5 for Ricky Williams. The scale of the package made the trade nearly impossible to justify.

headline: The 2025 Micah Parsons Trade: Green Bay Paid Two Firsts for a Prime Elite Pass Rusher
dek: Green Bay sent Dallas Kenny Clark and first-round picks in 2026 and 2027 for Micah Parsons. The Packers bought proven star power, while Dallas chose future flexibility.

headline: The 2026 Wanya Morris Trade: Atlanta Bought Tackle Depth for a One-Round Pick Swap
dek: Atlanta sent a 2027 sixth-rounder to Kansas City for Wanya Morris and a 2027 seventh, adding a young tackle with 16 NFL starts at a modest draft cost.

seoTitle: Daniel Faalele to Jaguars Trade Verdict | Giants-Jaguars
seoDescription: Jacksonville acquired Daniel Faalele from the Giants for a 2027 sixth-round pick after Patrick Mekari's back surgery. TradeVerdicts grades the deal and explains the roster, contract, and protection implications.
headline: Daniel Faalele to the Jaguars: Cheap Insurance with Real Upside
dek: Jacksonville paid only a 2027 sixth-round pick for an experienced 26-year-old guard after Patrick Mekari's back surgery, while the Giants converted a second-team lineman into future draft capital.

sections.heading: Why Jacksonville Moved Now
sections.body: The timing is the first reason this trade makes sense. Patrick Mekari's back surgery created an immediate need for experienced interior depth, and Jacksonville responded without surrendering a premium asset. Faalele has 66 regular-season appearances, 35 starts, and 34 consecutive starts at right guard over the previous two seasons. That is a substantial amount of NFL experience for the price of a future sixth-round selection.

sections.heading: The Contract Makes the Gamble Easier
sections.body: Jacksonville inherits only $1.215 million in base salary on Faalele's one-year, $1.4 million deal. That keeps the downside low. If he wins a starting job or becomes dependable injury insurance, the Jaguars receive useful snaps at a bargain cap number. If he does not, the financial commitment is small and the draft cost was already modest.

sections.heading: Why the Giants Could Move On
sections.body: Faalele followed John Harbaugh to New York but had been working with the second-team offense at left guard. The Giants had veteran Jon Runyan and 2026 first-round pick Francis Mauigoa positioned ahead of him, which made the roster math straightforward. Rather than keep a veteran reserve on a one-year contract, New York recovered a 2027 sixth-round pick.

sections.heading: Faalele Is Not a Clean Pass-Protection Fix
sections.body: The concern is pass protection. The reaction material supplied for this trade cites 30 pressures and four sacks allowed across 535 pass-blocking snaps last season. That helps explain why the Jaguars' grade stops at B+. Jacksonville is adding a legitimate NFL option, but not a player whose recent tape guarantees that the club's protection issues disappear.

sections.heading: The Run-Game Case Is Stronger
sections.body: Faalele's massive frame and starting history make the run-game fit easier to understand. Jacksonville's official announcement highlighted that he blocked for Baltimore offenses that ranked first in rushing in 2024 and second in 2025. Those team numbers are not an individual grade, but they show that Faalele has extensive experience functioning inside a productive, physical rushing environment.

sections.heading: What a Sixth-Round Pick Is Really Buying
sections.body: Late-round selections have value, but the expected return is uncertain. Jacksonville effectively exchanged a low-probability future asset for a known 26-year-old lineman with starting experience. The Giants preferred the opposite side of the equation: they did not need Faalele to start and therefore banked a future pick instead. Both decisions are rational, which is why the grade gap is only half a step.

sections.heading: Why the Pending Physical Matters
sections.body: The transaction is not fully complete until Faalele passes his physical. That qualifier belongs in the evaluation because Jacksonville is acquiring him specifically to strengthen an injury-hit position group. A failed or concerning physical would change the entire risk profile. Until the condition is satisfied, the verdict should be read as a trade-day grade on the agreed terms.

sections.heading: Final Verdict: Slight Jaguars Edge
sections.body: Jacksonville earns a B+ and the early win because experienced offensive-line depth at $1.215 million in base salary is worth a future sixth when the roster has an immediate injury need. New York earns a B for converting a second-team player into a pick. The Jaguars take on more performance risk, but they also acquire the asset capable of helping right away. If Faalele cannot improve Jacksonville's protection or the physical changes the deal, this verdict should be revisited.

seoTitle: Deion Jones-Zamir White Trade Grades | TradeVerdicts
headline: 49ers-Saints Deion Jones-Zamir White Trade: San Francisco Gets the Slight Edge
dek: San Francisco traded running back Zamir White to New Orleans for veteran linebacker Deion Jones, with both teams repurposing roster-bubble depth to address more immediate needs.

seoTitle: Kayshon Boutte Trade Grades: Texans vs. Patriots | TradeVerdicts
headline: Texans-Patriots Kayshon Boutte Trade: Houston Wins the Immediate Value
dek: Houston acquired Kayshon Boutte from New England for safety Jaylen Reed and a 2028 seventh-round pick, adding an immediate outside receiver after Jayden Higgins' season-ending ACL injury.

seoTitle: Joshua Ezeudu Trade Grades: Chiefs vs. Giants | TradeVerdicts
headline: Chiefs-Giants Joshua Ezeudu Trade: Kansas City Gets the Slight Edge
dek: Kansas City acquired offensive lineman Joshua Ezeudu from the Giants for a 2028 seventh-round pick, adding experienced guard-tackle depth at a minimal future cost.

seoTitle: Tutu Atwell-Jarquez Hunter Trade Grades | TradeVerdicts
headline: Dolphins-Rams Tutu Atwell-Jarquez Hunter Trade: Miami Gets the Slight Edge
dek: Miami sent Tutu Atwell back to Los Angeles for second-year running back Jarquez Hunter in a late-preseason player-for-player exchange.
